## TrueTime for Jira

Forge-native timesheets for Jira. One-click timers, weekly timesheets, approvals, and Tempo migration. Your data never leaves Atlassian.

**Beta:** TrueTime is in beta. Full release is planned for Q4 2026. [Join the beta](/truetime/beta.html).

**Free for up to 10 users.** $2.99 per user per month above that. Marketplace bills per Jira site user.

## sla.md


This page states the support service levels for Infralicious apps.
It covers TrueTime for Jira.

## Support Channel

Support runs through the [contact form](/contact.html).
Paid-tier customers also get direct phone access.
We share phone numbers privately with paid-tier customers only.
We never publish phone numbers on this site.

## Response Times

We respond to support requests within 1 business day.
Paid subscribers receive priority support.
Incoming triage and serious bugs take precedence over other requests.
Bug reports and feature requests have no fixed response time.
We review them regularly for future releases.

## Support Hours

Support hours are Monday to Friday.
Hours follow Central Time business hours.
US public holidays are excluded.

## Beta Status

TrueTime is in beta.
During beta, these targets are goals, not guarantees.
Support is best effort during beta.

## Platform Availability

Infralicious apps run on Atlassian Forge.
Atlassian operates the platform and its availability.
We target 99.9% uptime. That target is not a guarantee.
This page sets no contractual uptime commitment.

## Changes

We may update this page.
The date below states the current version.

## privacy.md


# Privacy Policy for Infralicious

**Last updated:** 2026-10-18

Infralicious ("we", "us") builds software for teams.
Contact: use the [contact form](/contact.html).

## What This Policy Covers

This policy covers all apps that Infralicious builds.
Each app also has its own policy page.
The app page lists the data that the app stores.
This page states the shared rules.

## What Data We Collect

Our apps run on the platforms you already use.
They store data on that platform's infrastructure.
We operate no separate database for app data.

Our apps do not collect analytics.
Our apps use no tracking pixels.
Our apps use no cookies for advertising.
We do not sell your data.
We do not share your data with third parties.

## Where Data Is Stored

App data stays on the host platform's infrastructure.
For Atlassian apps, data stays in Atlassian systems.
We send no app data to servers outside the host platform.

## Data Retention

Each app deletes its stored data when you uninstall it.
The host platform controls the deletion.
See the app policy page for app-specific retention rules.

## Your Rights (GDPR/CCPA)

- **Access:** You can view your data in the app.
- **Deletion:** Uninstall the app to delete its stored data.
- **Portability:** Each app offers export where it applies.
- **No sale:** We do not sell, share, or disclose your data to third parties.

## Third Parties

We use no third-party analytics, advertising, or data processing services for app data.

Messages sent through the contact form pass through Google Forms before they reach us.

## Security

Our apps run within the host platform's sandbox.
We inherit the host platform's security certifications.
We store no credentials for app data access.

## Changes

We will update this policy when our data practices change.
Material changes will be announced via the app listing.

## Contact

For privacy questions or data requests, use the [contact form](/contact.html).

## App Policies

- [TrueTime for Jira privacy policy](/truetime/privacy.html)

# Terms of Service for Infralicious

**Last updated:** 2026-10-27

These terms govern your use of apps built by Infralicious ("we", "us").
Contact: use the [contact form](/contact.html).
Each app also has its own terms page.
The app page states app-specific pricing and trial terms.
These terms state the shared rules.

## 1. License

We grant you a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use our apps within your host platform, subject to these terms and your subscription tier.

## 2. Acceptable Use

You agree not to:
- Reverse-engineer or attempt to extract an app's source code
- Use an app to violate any law or regulation
- Interfere with the operation of an app or its host platform
- Resell or sublicense an app without our written permission

## 3. Data

You retain full ownership of your data.
We claim no rights over your data.
On cancellation, export your data before you uninstall the app.
After uninstall, app preferences are deleted.
Data stored in the host platform remains.

## 4. Service Availability

Our apps run on their host platforms.
We target 99.9% uptime. That target is not a guarantee.
The SLA sets no contractual uptime commitment.
Host platform outages are outside our control.

## 5. Limitation of Liability

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW:
- Our apps are provided "as is" without warranties of any kind
- Our total liability is limited to the fees you paid in the prior 12 months
- We are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages
- We are not liable for data loss in the host platform (your admin controls backups)

## 6. Support

Use the [contact form](/contact.html).
We aim to respond within 1 business day.
Paid subscribers receive priority support.

## 7. Termination

You may cancel at any time by uninstalling the app or cancelling your subscription.
We may suspend service for violation of these terms, with 30 days notice except for serious abuse.

## 8. Changes

We may update these terms.
Material changes will be announced 30 days in advance via the app listing.
Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance.

## 9. Governing Law

These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Nebraska, USA, without regard to conflict of law principles.

## faq.md


## What is TrueTime for Jira?

TrueTime is Forge-native timesheets for Jira.
Log time on issues. See weeks at a glance. Approve weeks with one click.

## Where does my time data live?

In your Jira. Worklogs are native Jira worklogs.
Only a running timer lives in Forge Storage.
TrueTime has no servers. We cannot see, sell, or lose your data.

## How much does TrueTime cost?

Free for up to 10 users. $2.99 per user per month above that.
Marketplace bills per Jira site user.
Example: 200 Jira site users cost $598 per month.

## How do I migrate from Tempo?

Export Tempo data to CSV. Import the file into TrueTime.
Your history moves with you. Read the [migration guide](/truetime/migration.html).

## Does TrueTime work on Jira Server or Data Center?

No. TrueTime is Cloud only.

## What happens to my data if I uninstall?

Worklogs stay in Jira. Billable flags stay in Jira.
A running timer is lost. Nothing else changes.

## How fast is support?

We reply within 1 business day, Monday to Friday, Central Time, except US holidays.
Paid subscribers get priority. See our [support SLA](/sla.html).

## Is TrueTime in beta?

Yes. Features may change. Full release is planned for Q4 2026.
[Join the beta](/truetime/beta.html).

## calculator.md


Tempo bills per Jira seat. TrueTime bills per Jira site user.
Marketplace bills both apps by site size, not by time tracker.
Enter your site size. See the difference.

<p id="result"></p>



Example: 200 Jira site users. Tempo costs $1,042 per month. TrueTime costs $598 per month. You save $444 per month, $5,328 per year.

Price is USD 2.99 per user per month for all tiers above 10 users.
Tempo price comes from its public Marketplace listing, checked October 2026.

## truetime/index.md


**Beta:** TrueTime is in beta. Features may change. Full release is planned for Q4 2026. [Join the beta](/truetime/beta.html).
{: .notice--warning}

TrueTime is a Forge-native timesheet app for Jira.
Your data never leaves Atlassian.
TrueTime has no servers.

## Key features

- **One-click timers.** Open a Jira issue. Click Start. Click Stop. The app creates a native Jira worklog.
- **Weekly timesheets.** See your week at a glance. Log time manually. Edit entries. Delete mistakes.
- **One-click approvals.** Submit your week with one click. Your manager approves or rejects.
- **Billable tracking.** Mark time as billable or non-billable. The flag stays in Jira. It survives uninstall.
- **Excel export.** One click. Real .xlsx file. Includes hours, billable flags, project totals.
- **Tempo import via CSV.** Export Tempo data to CSV. Upload it into TrueTime. Your history moves with you.
- **Teams.** Create teams, manage members, and control who can approve timesheets.
- **Free for up to 10 users.** $2.99 per user per month above that.

## truetime/user-guide.md


**Beta:** TrueTime is in beta. Features may change. Full release is planned for Q4 2026.
{: .notice--warning}

## Log time

### Option 1: Timer

Use the timer on any Jira issue.

1. Open a Jira issue.
2. Click **View app actions**.
3. Click **TrueTime**.
4. Click **Start timer**.
5. Add a comment if you want.
6. Set **Billable** on or off.
7. Click **Stop**.
8. The app creates a native Jira worklog.

### Option 2: Manual entry

Enter time manually in the timesheet view.

1. Open **TrueTime Timesheet**.
2. Add an entry with these fields:
   - **Issue key**. Example: `PROJ-123`.
   - **Date**. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.
   - **Hours**. Example: `2.5`.
   - **Comment**. Optional.
   - **Billable**. Default is on.
3. Save the entry.

### View your week

1. Open the **Timesheet** tab.
2. The tab shows all entries for the current week.
3. Use **Prev** and **Next** to change weeks.
4. Edit or delete an entry from the grid.

### Draft my week

Use **Draft my week** on the My Time tab.
The app drafts entries from recent tickets.
The app drafts entries from work you touched but did not time.
The app drafts entries for empty days.
Nothing saves until you confirm.
Review each draft first.
Edit or discard a draft before you save it.

### Timesheet tips

- **Keyboard shortcuts**: `←` / `→` switch weeks, `N` starts a new entry.
- **Copy last week**: one button copies last week's entries as drafts. Review them, then save all or discard.
- **Overtime flags**: days over 8h and weeks over 40h get a badge.
- Weekends are shaded in the grid. Hours round to the nearest 15 minutes.
- Deleting a worklog removes it at once.

## Approvals

### Submit your week

1. Click the **Approvals** tab.
2. Click **Submit for approval**.
3. Your approver sees it in their queue.

### Approve or reject

Approvers manage the queue in the **Approvals** tab.

1. Open **Pending approvals**.
2. Click **Approve** or **Reject**.
3. A rejection needs a reason. The author can resubmit after a rejection.

### Set up approvers

1. Open the **Approvals** tab.
2. Find the **Approvers** section.
3. Search by name or email, then add the approver.
4. Until at least one approver exists, approvals stay disabled.

## Teams

- Create a team with a name and members.
- Add members one by one, or import members from a Jira group.
- Roles are Team Lead and Member. Custom roles are possible.
- Team leads manage members and settings.
- Team leads can view team worklogs.
- Team leads can approve team members' timesheets.
- Team leads can manage team worklogs.
- Team leads can view a team week.
- Only team leads or the team creator can delete a team.
- Deleted teams go to trash for 30 days. Restore a team from the Deleted teams section. After 30 days, the team is gone for good.

### Import members from a Jira group

1. Open the team.
2. Search for a Jira group by name.
3. Import the group members into the team.
4. The import copies current members as individuals.
5. The app stores no link to the Jira group.
6. Later Jira group changes do not change the team.
7. Check member roles after import.
8. Set Team Lead roles as needed.

## Admin settings

Open settings from **Atlassian Administration → Apps → TrueTime → Configure**, or from the **Settings** tab inside the Timesheet page.

### Auto-timers

- A timer starts when an issue moves to a selected status.
- The timer stops and writes a worklog when the issue moves to an inactive status.
- Pick statuses from the dropdowns. Defaults: active `In Progress`, inactive `Done, Closed, Resolved`.

### Lockable periods

- Lock a week so nobody can log, edit, or delete worklogs in it.
- Pick any date with the date picker. The whole week gets locked.
- Unlock a week at any time.

### Non-ticketed work

- Set a placeholder issue for work without a ticket, such as meetings or admin work.
- Type an issue key. A preview shows the summary so you can confirm the issue.
- Users then pick **Non-ticketed** in the log work form.

### Board card display

- Show total hours logged on each Jira board card.
- Create a native **Number** custom field in Jira first (Jira Settings → Issues → Custom fields).
- Pick the field from the dropdown, then add it to your board's Card Layout.
- Totals sync on worklog create, update, and delete.
- If your field is missing from the dropdown, use the **Refresh fields** button.

### Custom attributes

- Add extra fields on every worklog, such as activity type, location, or client code.
- Type is a dropdown: text, number, dropdown, checkbox, date.
- Custom attributes are stored as worklog properties. They survive uninstall.
- Deleting an attribute asks for confirmation first.

### Private labeling

- Rename the app and set a brand color and logo URL.
- Use the color picker or type a hex code. The swatch previews live.

## Reports

1. Click the **Report** tab.
2. The tab shows hours grouped by project.
3. Click **Download Excel (.xlsx)** for a spreadsheet.
4. Click **Download CSV** for a plain-text export. Excel, Google Sheets, and Apple Numbers can read CSV files.

## FAQ

**Where is my data?**

Your data is in Jira. Time entries are native Jira worklogs. The app sends no data to external servers.

**What happens if I uninstall TrueTime?**

Your worklogs stay in Jira. You lose only running timers, approval records, and app preferences.

**Why is there a 1-minute minimum?**

Jira requires a minimum of 60 seconds for worklogs. The app rounds up shorter timers.

**Who approves my week?**

Your Jira admin configures approvers. Ask your admin if you are not sure.

**Can I use TrueTime on a phone?**

TrueTime does not appear in the native Jira mobile app.
Forge issue panels and global pages have no mobile route.
Use a desktop browser for TrueTime.
We do not promise a mobile workaround yet.

## truetime/migration.md


**Beta:** TrueTime is in beta. Features may change. Full release is planned for Q4 2026.
{: .notice--warning}

Move your Tempo history into TrueTime with a CSV export.
Migration is CSV-only. TrueTime makes no API calls to Tempo.
Your Tempo token is never needed. Your data stays in Atlassian.

## Steps

1. Export your worklogs from Tempo to CSV.
2. Open **TrueTime Timesheet**.
3. Open the **Migration** tab.
4. Upload the CSV file.
5. Check the import result. The app skips invalid rows and reports each skip.
6. The app skips duplicates automatically.

## CSV format

You can upload a Tempo export as is. The app reads the Tempo columns:
Work Item Key, Logged Hours or Logged Seconds, Work Date, Work Description,
and Billable Seconds.

A simple format also works. The header is: `Date, Issue, Hours, Comment`.

Example row: `2026-10-05, PROJ-123, 2.5, Sprint work`.

## What moves with you

- Dates, issue keys, hours, comments, and the billable flag move into TrueTime.
- Imported entries become native Jira worklogs.
- Entries appear in timesheets, approvals, and reports like any other entry.

## What to know

- Migration is CSV-only. There is no Tempo API import.
- Your Tempo token is never needed and never asked for.
- Validate the import result before you uninstall Tempo.
- Keep your Tempo CSV file until you confirm the import looks right.

## truetime/api.md


**Beta:** TrueTime is in beta. Features may change. Full release is planned for Q4 2026.
{: .notice--warning}

TrueTime entries are native Jira worklogs.
You can create them with the Jira REST API.
Scripts and AI agents can use the same calls.
TrueTime has no public API of its own today.

## What you need

- Your Jira site URL, for example `https://your-site.atlassian.net`.
- An Atlassian API token for your account.
  Create one at id.atlassian.com under Security, then API tokens.
- An issue key to log time on.

Keep the token secret. The token acts with your full account rights.

## Create an entry

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -u "you@example.com:YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://your-site.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/MP-15/worklog" \
  -d '{
    "timeSpentSeconds": 28800,
    "started": "2026-10-12T09:00:00.000+0000",
    "comment": {
      "type": "doc",
      "version": 1,
      "content": [
        { "type": "paragraph", "content": [
          { "type": "text", "text": "Design review" } ] }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

The call returns HTTP 201 and the new worklog ID.
`started` sets the day and the start time, in your account timezone.

Read, update, and delete use the same base path:

- Read: `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/worklog`
- Update: `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/worklog/{worklogId}`
- Delete: `DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/worklog/{worklogId}`

## What this path skips

The app checks each entry at write time. The Jira API path skips these checks:

1. **Future dates.** The app rejects an entry dated in the future.
2. **24 hour cap.** The app rejects an entry over 24 hours.
3. **Locked periods.** The app refuses writes into a locked week.
4. **Submitted weeks.** The app refuses writes into a submitted or approved week. An API write lands anyway and then disagrees with the submitted counts. Do not write into a submitted week.
5. **Overlap warnings.** The app warns when two entries overlap in time.
6. **Comment cleanup.** The app trims and sanitizes comment text.
7. **Delete audit.** The app records a snapshot of a deleted entry. An API delete leaves no snapshot.

Jira still applies its own rules. You need worklog permission on the issue.

## Billable and other flags

The app stores flags as worklog properties.
An entry with no properties reads as non-billable in the app.
Set the billable flag with a second call:

```bash
curl -s -X PUT \
  -u "you@example.com:YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://your-site.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/MP-15/worklog/10153/properties/truetime-billable" \
  -d '{ "billable": true }'
```

Other keys: `truetime-capex-opex` with body `{ "type": "capex" }`, and `truetime-real-started` with body `{ "realStart": true }` when `started` is the true start time.

## What the API cannot do

Week submission lives in the app, not in Jira.
No API call can submit, approve, or withdraw a week.
Use the Team tab in the TrueTime page for those steps.

## truetime/privacy.md


# Privacy Policy for TrueTime for Jira

This document covers TrueTime for Jira by Infralicious.

**Effective date:** October 11, 2026
**Last updated:** 2026-10-18

TrueTime for Jira ("TrueTime", "we", "us") is built by Infralicious.
Contact: use the [contact form](/contact.html).

## What Data We Collect

**Time tracking data stays in Jira.** When you log time with TrueTime,
we create native Jira worklogs. Your time entries, comments, and issue
associations live in your Jira instance, not on our servers. If you
uninstall TrueTime, every hour you ever logged stays in Jira.

**What TrueTime stores** (in Atlassian Forge Storage, on Atlassian infrastructure):
- Running timer state (issue key, start time) - so timers survive tab close
- App preferences (week start day, branding, auto-timer config, approver lists)
- Team definitions and memberships
- Approval records (submitted weeks, decisions)
- Custom attribute definitions
- Cached reference data (temporary)

**What TrueTime does NOT collect:**
- No analytics, no tracking pixels, no cookies for advertising
- No personal data beyond what Jira already provides (display name, email for approver lists)
- No data is sent to any server outside Atlassian infrastructure

## Where Data Is Stored

All data is stored on Atlassian infrastructure via Forge Storage and Forge KVS.
No TrueTime data leaves Atlassian's systems. We operate no separate database.

## Data Retention

- Timer state: deleted when the timer stops or after 24 hours of inactivity
- Preferences: retained until you change them or uninstall the app
- On uninstall: all Forge Storage data is deleted by Atlassian automatically

## Your Rights (GDPR/CCPA)

- **Access:** All your data is visible in the app's settings and in Jira
- **Deletion:** Uninstall the app to delete all stored preferences. Delete Jira worklogs directly in Jira.
- **Portability:** Export your time data as CSV/Excel from the Reports tab at any time
- **No sale:** We do not sell, share, or disclose your data to third parties

## Third Parties

TrueTime integrates only with your Jira instance via Atlassian's Forge platform.
We use no third-party analytics, advertising, or data processing services.

## Security

TrueTime runs entirely within Atlassian's Forge sandbox. We inherit Atlassian's
security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001). All API calls use Atlassian's
authenticated Forge bridge - no credentials are stored by TrueTime.

## Changes

We will update this policy when our data practices change. Material changes
will be announced via the Atlassian Marketplace listing.

## Contact

For privacy questions or data requests, use the [contact form](/contact.html).

Messages sent through the contact form pass through Google Forms before they reach us.

This page alone states the full policy for TrueTime.

## truetime/switch.md


Tempo is the big timesheet app for Jira. TrueTime is the Forge-native alternative.
This page compares the two on facts that matter to buyers.

| Topic | TrueTime | Tempo |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly price | $2.99 per Jira site user, free to 10 users | $5.21 per Jira seat |
| Billing base | Every Jira site user | Every Jira seat |
| Data location | Atlassian only (Forge) | Vendor servers |
| Platform | Jira Cloud only | Jira Cloud and Data Center |
| Support first response | Within 1 business day | Within 1 business day |
| Team delete | 30-day trash with restore | Archive, no restore |
| Approvals | Simple submit, approve, reject | Full approval workflows |
| Migration | Import Tempo CSV in minutes | Export CSV any time |

Example: 200 Jira site users. Tempo costs $1,042 per month. TrueTime costs $598 per month. You save $444 per month.

Tempo prices and SLA come from its public Marketplace listing and support pages, checked October 2026.
Tempo wins on platform range and approval depth. TrueTime wins on price and data location.

[Try TrueTime in beta](/truetime/beta.html). Read the [migration guide](/truetime/migration.html).
